documents.title: Lucky Thirteen: Breaking the TLS and DTLS Record Protocols

review.title: Lucky 13 Attack
repairs: Restored all 4 source superscripts as unambiguous caret notation, checked against each original sup element; unchanged ordinary byte counts and dates.
Restored missing final For more information paragraph and research-paper link from frozen source.

digest_review.evidence: TLS and DTLS CBC decryption runs measurably faster when a record carries at least two bytes of valid padding, because the 13-byte MAC header aligns hash compression blocks differently. Timing TLS error messages on a LAN and averaging out jitter recovers a plaintext block in about 2^23 sessions, fewer with base64 or BEAST-style tricks; DTLS falls in a single session. Verified against source mechanism and corrected source numerical complexities.

documents.title: On the Security of RC4 in TLS

review.title: Weaknesses in RC4
repairs: Restored all 9 source superscripts as unambiguous caret notation, checked against each original sup element; unchanged ordinary byte counts and dates.

digest_review.evidence: Measured the keystream biases of RC4 as used in TLS and turned them into plaintext recovery. A single-byte-bias attack over the first 256 keystream bytes recovers 220 bytes of a repeated plaintext from roughly 2^30 sessions, and a double-byte (Fluhrer-McGrew) attack works within one connection. The single-byte attack carries to WPA/TKIP because of its per-packet keys. Verified against source mechanism and corrected source numerical complexities.

documents.title: Prepare(): Introducing novel Exploitation Techniques in WordPress

review.title: Prepare(): Introducing novel Exploitation Techniques in WordPress
review.description: WordPress before 4.8.3 allowed SQL injection when prepare() was applied twice to input containing placeholders. Its fix introduced secret percent-sign tokens: when a WP_Query containing those tokens is serialized for transient caching, query() restores percent signs after serialization and shortens the stored string without updating its length prefix. Controlled later data can then inject a PHP object, illustrated through an authenticated WooCommerce RCE path.
